git show 89deae6 --stat | head -5; echo "---"; git show 89deae6:$(git show 89deae6 --stat | grep -o 'journals/[^ ]*\.md' | head -1) 2>/dev/null | head -80

cd journals && python3 -c "
import yaml, sys
with open('2026-11-02-chaos-toggle-503s.md') as f:
    content = f.read()
# extract frontmatter between first and second '---'
parts = content.split('---\n', 2)
fm = parts[1]
data = yaml.safe_load(fm)
print('YAML parsed OK')
print('top-level keys:', list(data.keys()))
" 2>&1 || echo "PYTHON_FAILED"

cd journals && for n in 5 6 7 8 15 20 26 32 40 45 50 56 62 70 76 81 86 91 100 106 107 108 109 110; do c=$(sed -n "${n}p" 2026-11-02-chaos-toggle-503s.md | grep -o '"' | wc -l); echo "line $n: $c quotes"; done

result_tail:
(infra-process, interfaces, software-defect) all converged on the same cause. No unhandled exceptions, no restart, no memory growth — ruling out a code bug or resource exhaustion. An adversarial judge flagged that the 0.4 rate was only self-reported by the toggle's own log line, so I pulled the full request tally: 4 failures out of 10 post-toggle requests, an exact match.

**Open items (in the journal's Gaps):** no visibility into who/what flipped the switch, and business traffic stopped after ~19 seconds so I can't confirm fresh user impact beyond the toggle still reading "on" at conclusion.
